title_as_printed: Dietary fatty acids and risk for Alzheimer's disease, dementia, and mild cognitive impairment: A prospective cohort meta-analysis

correct_pdf.title_as_printed: Association of dietary choline intake with incidence of dementia, Alzheimer disease, and mild cognitive impairment: a large population-based prospective cohort study
correct_pdf.how_found: read-only title scan of the first two pages of all 1,679 PDFs under downloads/; single hit
correct_pdf.note: The pack extract is Zhu et al. 2021, Nutrition 90:111355 (fatty-acid meta-analysis). The registry row describes the choline cohort study, so blind codes and judgements below are against the correct PDF; page numbers refer to it.

blind_codes_pack_extract.paper: Zhu et al. 2021, Nutrition 90:111355, dietary fatty acids and AD/dementia/MCI, prospective cohort meta-analysis

Task_Type.reason: UK Biobank prospective cohort; Cox hazard ratios and logistic odds ratios relating dietary choline to incident dementia/AD/MCI and to baseline cognitive performance. No classifier. It is epidemiology (T6), but the core result is an exposure-outcome association, which the template also admits as T4 (correlational). The registry's T4 is one of the two readings.
Task_Type.quote: The objective of this study was to explore the associations between dietary choline intake and the incidence of dementia, Alzheimer disease (AD), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and current cognitive performance in the United Kingdom Biobank cohort.

Category.reason: The data domain is a population cohort: 24-h dietary recall questionnaires (choline estimated from a USDA food-composition table), hospital and death-record ICD codes, and touchscreen cognitive tests. No CSF, plasma, genomic or omic data are analysed; the limitations state that circulating choline was not measured (p.8). C3 has no basis as a data domain, and the primary domain C5 is missing. That choline is a molecule is a feature of the exposure, not of the data.
Category.quote: Dietary choline intake was categorized into quartiles of consumption based on 24-h dietary recalls, with units expressed as milligrams per day.

Validation_Type.reason: Association analysis (Cox, logistic, restricted cubic splines); no predictive model is validated.

Sample_N_Approx.quote: Among 125,594 participants (55.8% female), with a mean age of 56.1 y (range: 40–70 years) at baseline and a median follow-up of 11.8 y

Publication_Year.reason: Online 7 November 2024; issue Am J Clin Nutr 121 (2025) 5-13. Registry uses the issue year.
